[1/2] Plan: close the two store-hygiene gaps flagged in the PR #8 verification - ResultStore.prune(now) removes expired records from the in-memory index and persists; load() lazily drops an expired record and a record whose .bin rebuild target is gone, persisting the healed index (open stays read-only)

impact_assessment.why: index.json grows without bound in long-lived stores and deleted .bin files left phantom records forever
impact_assessment.benefits: bounded index file, self-healing store, explicit prune API for future consumers
impact_assessment.risks: contract: load() of an expired/lost result now also deletes its record (still returns None as before); dependency: none (stdlib); concurrency: last-writer-wins unchanged; state: index.json format unchanged, no migration
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests, slice re-read of load()/persist paths, 32/32 target suites then 5/5 gates before publish

[1/2] Plan: post-merge verification of main (65ef1b1..90b1dec) - merge clean (6 files, no deletions), suite 2610 passed, gates clean. One tightening remains: _load_index accepts arbitrary result ids and stored paths from index.json without revalidation; fix by validating each record id with _resolve_target at load so a tampered index is refused as a whole (consistent with the version-refusal contract)

impact_assessment.why: A tampered index record currently persists forever inside _index and is only refused at serve time
impact_assessment.benefits: index.json becomes fully self-validating on open; stored path derived from the validated id, eliminating the persisted-path drift
impact_assessment.risks: contract: an index containing any unvalidated id now refuses the whole store open (was: silent acceptance, refusal only when loading that id); dependency: none; concurrency: unchanged; state: format unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first test, slice re-read of _load_index, 35/35 target suites + full gates before publish
